exercise.name: Dumbbell Bench Dip (dumbbell on the lap)
aliases: Bench dip with a dumbbell on the lap

reference.title: Bench Dip (knees bent)
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Body-weight bench dip, knees bent; the dumbbell resting on the lap is the usual way to load it. Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.3 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell once 12 controlled reps are easy; keep the range at upper arms parallel

cues.text: Hands on the edge of the bench beside the hips, fingers forward; feet out, knees bent; a partner (or you, before you lift off) sets a dumbbell across the thighs near the knees; arms straight.
Breathe in and bend the elbows straight back, lowering the hips close to the bench.
Stop when the upper arms are about parallel to the floor; shoulders down, chest open.
Breathe out and push through the palms to straighten the arms.
Arms straight but not locked; the dumbbell stays still on the lap; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Stop at upper arms about parallel to the floor; the bench dip already takes the shoulder to the end of its extension range (McKenzie 2022).

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders shrugging up and rolling forward
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down and back, chest open.

mistakes.mistake: Hips drifting away from the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the back close to the bench edge as you lower.
Let the arms do the work; the feet only balance.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbell sliding toward the hips or off the lap
mistakes.fix: Set it near the knees, across both thighs, and keep the shins vertical so the thighs stay level.

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; with the hands gripping the bench edge the elbows are bent about 100-120 degrees when the upper arms reach parallel (clinical opinion); elbow flexion on the bench dip was less than on the bar dip (McKenzie 2022)
Peak shoulder extension in a self-selected bench dip was about 88 degrees, 101% of the maximal range measured in each lifter, more than bar or ring dips (McKenzie 2022)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm angle to the floor
kinematics.norm: Stop with the upper arms about parallel to the floor (clinical opinion)
Hips move straight down and up close to the bench (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #012912, Bench Dip (knees bent), video (movement reference)
McKenzie, Crowley-McHattan, Meir, Whitting and Volschenk 2022, bench, bar, and ring dips: do kinematics and muscle activity differ? (Int J Environ Res Public Health 19(20):13211; PMC9603242)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

cautions: Shoulder: the bench dip takes the shoulder to about the end of its extension range, which can strain the front of the shoulder capsule; the study authors advised against it in regular training or rehabilitation (McKenzie 2022). Keep the range short (upper arms parallel at most).
Skip it with a history of shoulder instability or pain at the front of the shoulder.
Use a stable bench that cannot slide or tip.
Lift the dumbbell off the lap (or have a partner take it) before you stand up; never let it roll off onto the feet.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range, or switch to a close-grip push-up or a cable pushdown.
Wrist discomfort: turn the fingers slightly out.
progressions: Straight legs with a plate on the lap.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows to lift the body. Peak triceps EMG was lower on the bench dip (0.83 mV) than on bar (1.04) or ring dips (1.05) (McKenzie 2022); in another comparison dips matched kickbacks and triangle push-ups (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows to lift the body. Peak triceps EMG was lower on the bench dip (0.83 mV) than on bar (1.04) or ring dips (1.05) (McKenzie 2022); in another comparison dips matched kickbacks and triangle push-ups (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Brings the arms forward from behind the body as you press up; significantly less active than on bar or ring dips (McKenzie 2022).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Brings the arms forward from behind the body as you press up; significantly less active than on bar or ring dips (McKenzie 2022).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Helps the front of the shoulder press up, with lower activity than on bar or ring dips (McKenzie 2022).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Helps the front of the shoulder press up, with lower activity than on bar or ring dips (McKenzie 2022).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the shoulders down and back, away from the ears (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the shoulders down and back, away from the ears (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades back so the chest stays open (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blades back so the chest stays open (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the hands on the edge of the bench.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the hands on the edge of the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk upright close to the bench.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the bent knees steady; the feet stay planted.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the bent knees steady; the feet stay planted.

phases.label: Arms straight, hands on the bench

guides.label: Hips lower close to the bench
